title: Hemolytic anemia: spherocytes + polychromasia + nucleated RBCs
vignette: A 32-year-old woman comes to the office due to worsening fatigue and exercise intolerance. She has no history of blood disorders. Physical examination shows mild mucosal pallor. Hemoglobin is 7.8 g/dL (normal 12-16). Peripheral blood smear is shown in the image and reveals spherocytes (small, dense red cells lacking central pallor), polychromatic red cells (larger, bluish red cells), and nucleated red blood cells. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's anemia?

clues.note: Fatigue and exercise intolerance are symptoms of anemia; the smear determines the mechanism.

clues.text: spherocytes (small, dense red cells lacking central pallor)
clues.note: Spherocytes (dense cells without central pallor) form when IgG-coated red cells are partially phagocytosed by splenic macrophages - a hallmark of immune-mediated hemolytic anemia.

clues.text: polychromatic red cells (larger, bluish red cells)
clues.note: Polychromatic (bluish) macrocytes are reticulocytes; increased reticulocytes indicate the marrow is appropriately responding to hemolysis/blood loss.
Nucleated red cells (very immature RBCs pushed into the blood) reflect a strong marrow response - together with spherocytes and polychromasia, they indicate hemolytic anemia.

whatMatters: Anemia (Hgb 7.8) with a smear showing SPHEROCYTES + POLYCHROMASIA (reticulocytosis) + NUCLEATED RBCs = HEMOLYTIC ANEMIA with a brisk marrow response (spherocytes suggest immune-mediated hemolysis). Answer B.
strategy: Read the smear as a triad of hemolysis: spherocytes (immune-mediated destruction), polychromasia/reticulocytosis and nucleated RBCs (compensatory marrow output). Reject iron deficiency (hypochromic microcytes), B12 deficiency (macro-ovalocytes + hypersegmented neutrophils), erythropoietin deficiency (no reticulocytosis, in CKD), and thrombotic microangiopathy (schistocytes, not spherocytes).

eliminations.label: Erythropoietin deficiency - no reticulocytosis
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: reduced EPO (e.g., chronic kidney disease) causing hypoproliferative anemia. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: the marrow can't respond, so the smear does NOT show increased reticulocytes (polychromasia) or nucleated RBCs, as seen here. ✅ Correct if: anemia of CKD with low reticulocyte count.

eliminations.label: Iron deficiency - hypochromic microcytes
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: iron deficiency causing microcytic, hypochromic anemia. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: its smear shows small, pale cells with increased central pallor - the OPPOSITE of dense spherocytes, and without brisk reticulocytosis. ✅ Correct if: microcytic hypochromic cells with low ferritin.

eliminations.label: Thrombotic microangiopathy - schistocytes, not spherocytes
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: microvascular clots shearing RBCs (TTP/HUS/DIC). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it produces SCHISTOCYTES (helmet/fragmented cells), not spherocytes, and usually thrombocytopenia. ✅ Correct if: schistocytes + thrombocytopenia + microangiopathy.

eliminations.label: Vitamin B12 deficiency - macrocytic, hypersegmented neutrophils (your pick)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: B12 deficiency causing megaloblastic (macrocytic) anemia. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: its smear shows macro-ovalocytes and HYPERSEGMENTED NEUTROPHILS with LOW reticulocytes - not spherocytes with brisk reticulocytosis. ✅ Correct if: macrocytosis + hypersegmented neutrophils + neuro symptoms.

reasoning: Anemia with a smear showing spherocytes + polychromasia + nucleated RBCs
Spherocytes indicate immune-mediated red cell destruction (partial splenic phagocytosis of IgG-coated cells)
Polychromasia (reticulocytosis) and nucleated RBCs show a brisk compensatory marrow response
mechanism: The peripheral smear points to hemolytic anemia with an appropriately hyperproliferative marrow. SPHEROCYTES - small, dense red cells lacking central pallor - arise when IgG-coated erythrocytes are partially phagocytosed by splenic macrophages (removing membrane and reducing surface area), classically in warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia (they also occur in hereditary spherocytosis). In response to ongoing red cell destruction (or blood loss), the bone marrow ramps up erythropoiesis and releases immature cells early: POLYCHROMATIC red cells are reticulocytes (bluish because residual ribosomal RNA takes up stain), and NUCLEATED red blood cells are very immature erythrocytes pushed into the circulation - both signal a strong marrow (reticulocyte) response. Together these findings define a hemolytic (reticulocyte-rich) anemia. This contrasts with hypoproliferative anemias (iron deficiency: microcytic/hypochromic; B12 deficiency: macro-ovalocytes + hypersegmented neutrophils; EPO deficiency: low reticulocytes) and with thrombotic microangiopathy (schistocytes).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Heme > hemolytic anemia smear: spherocytes (immune/hereditary), polychromasia/reticulocytosis, nucleated RBCs; contrast schistocytes (microangiopathy), hypersegmented neutrophils (B12), microcytes (iron).

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Spherocytes + polychromasia + nucleated RBCs = hemolysis with a brisk marrow response.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on spherocyte, polychromasia/reticulocyte, nucleated RBC, schistocyte, or hypersegmented neutrophil? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: B12 = macro-ovalocytes/hypersegmented neutrophils; iron = microcytic/hypochromic; EPO deficiency = low reticulocytes; TMA = schistocytes - not spherocytes.

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.text: On the smear: dense spherocytes without central pallor, bluish polychromatic macrocytes (reticulocytes), and a nucleated RBC. Anchor: 'spherocytes + reticulocytosis = hemolytic anemia.'

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: hemolytic anemia -> spherocytes (immune), ↑reticulocytes/polychromasia, nucleated RBCs, ↑LDH/indirect bilirubin, ↓haptoglobin.

keywords.back: Splenic macrophages partially phagocytose IgG-coated RBCs

firstAid.detail: Heme > iron (microcytic), B12 (hypersegmented), TMA (schistocytes), EPO deficiency (low retic).
firstAid.location: Heme > iron (microcytic), B12 (hypersegmented), TMA (schistocytes), EPO deficiency (low retic).

memoryHook: Dense spherocytes plus a flood of baby red cells (reticulocytes + nucleated RBCs) = the marrow scrambling to replace cells being destroyed - hemolysis.
